sources.overlap_strategy: Fetch the current official table in three separated windows, archive the source JSON, and overwrite only the same source-date CSV on an idempotent rerun.
sources.schedule_rationale: Jobs start at 12:20, 20:20, and 04:20 Beijing time and wait a random 0-20 minutes, so requests normally fall in three separated windows. The overnight run is a third recovery opportunity before the next normal 08:00 replacement. GitHub scheduler delays can move a run later. The source has no historical query, so a missed replacement day cannot be reconstructed from the official endpoint.

sources.schedule_rationale: A genuine rolling window with no day-file reset, so any single run recovers a full 24h. Three runs 8h apart mean two consecutive failures still lose no data.

sources.overlap_strategy: Each fetch returns every hourly point since 00:00 JST, so a later run supersedes earlier ones for that day; merged on (station_id, observed_at). NOTE: 手取川ダム is also delivered from MLIT/OpenGov and must be de-duplicated at the delivery layer; the other 11 dams are new.
sources.schedule_rationale: The day file accumulates hourly points from 00:00 JST and resets at midnight, and past dates 404. The 23:50 JST run captures all 24 points on its own; the 17:50, 11:50 and 05:50 runs each secure everything up to that hour should the primary fail.

sources.overlap_strategy: Append-only accumulator keyed on (reservoir_code, lastUpdate); re-reading the same published day adds nothing.
sources.schedule_rationale: The API publishes one value per day via its own lastUpdate field. Its 30-point series cannot be dated -- the per-series dt is a generator cursor that decrements one hour per series in listing order -- so no history is retrievable and a missed day is unrecoverable. Captured twice daily with a wide separation so one failed run does not cost a day.

sources.overlap_strategy: Two endpoints per station: past (7d hourly, 貯水位/流入量/全放流量 only) and current (~50h hourly, adds 貯水量 and percentages). Merged on (obs_fcd, observed_at), current filling storage over the past window's tail. Consecutive runs overlap by 6 days for the core variables and ~26h for storage. By normalised name it overlaps the MLIT/OpenGov delivery (126/127) and the seven per-prefecture feeds (199/209) — de-duplicate at the delivery layer; ~596 stations (583 distinct names) are new. Note 坂本ダム and other repeated Japanese dam names occur at several sites, so de-duplication must key on obs_fcd plus prefecture, never on name alone.
sources.schedule_rationale: The 7-day past window makes the three core variables robust to six consecutive failures; the ~50h current window makes storage tolerate one. Daily is the cadence the shorter window dictates.

sources.overlap_strategy: Append-only accumulator keyed on (dam_jp, bulletin date parsed from the PDF); polling daily on a monthly bulletin simply re-reads the same issue until a new one appears.
sources.schedule_rationale: Only the current issue is kept: older dated filenames 404 (verified r80801/r80701/r80601/r80815 on 2026-09-09) and the Internet Archive holds three snapshots under three naming schemes, which is not a usable backfill. The bulletin is monthly but neither the publication day nor the filename convention is stable, so the landing page is polled daily and the link is read from it rather than constructed. Daily polling of a monthly issue gives far more than two capture opportunities.

sources.overlap_strategy: Append-only accumulator keyed on (prefecture, dam_jp, observed_at); a repeated observation time is written once. The accumulated file IS the series because the source publishes no history.
sources.schedule_rationale: No backfill path exists: historical queries return zero dam rows and the Wayback Machine holds no snapshot of this servlet, so anything a run misses is lost permanently. The source advances every 10-30 minutes, which is a continuous signal rather than a discrete expiring publication; the intended product is therefore an HOURLY sampled series. Running every 30 minutes gives each hourly slot two capture opportunities, so a single failed or delayed run does not create a hole. A twice-daily cadence would capture 2 of roughly 48 daily observations and is not appropriate here.

Fukushima and Yamaguchi advance hourly, so hourly capture with a 2-hour maximum gap gives each hourly observation two chances before it is replaced. The daily sites cost nothing extra because repeated observation dates are deduplicated.

sources.overlap_strategy: The endpoint returns the whole retained table on every call, so one successful run recovers every day since the last one; records merge by reference_date.
sources.schedule_rationale: Twice a month (1st and 16th), 06:20 and 17:20 Africa/Maputo. Because the full retained table is served on every call - records back to 2025-03-06 are still present - nothing is lost between polls, so a fortnightly cadence collects the same data as a daily one at a fraction of the cost. The second run on each collection day is the recovery opportunity.
